A roo is a binding. Equal parts butter and flour, cooked together before you add the liquid.
Fifty grams of butter. Fifty grams of flour. Always weigh. Never measure by volume.
Melt the butter on a gentle heat. Add the flour all at once. Whisk until the paste is smooth, with no lumps.
White roo: two to three minutes, no colour. That is the base of bay-sha-mel.
Blond roo: a pale gold and a hint of hazelnut. That is the base of vell-oo-tay.
Brown roo: darker, toasted. That is the base of ess-pan-yole. The more it colours, the less it thickens, so you use a little more.
The liquid comes afterwards. Milk or stock, little by little. The roo is cooked first.
The heat knocks out the amylase in raw flour. The fat coats the starch, so it will not clump.
